The designed MIM structure is composed of a five-layer stack of Silver - Fr4 - Silver - Gallium Arsenide - Silver.
The thickness of each silver layer is 0.1 μm, the Fr4 dielectric layer is 0.2 μm, and the GaAs dielectric layer is 0.1 μm.
The periodic dimensions of the unit cell are Sx = Sy = 2.4 μm, and the radius of the silver disk layer is 0.3 μm.
The designed MIM structure exhibits three absorption peaks at wavelengths of 1.3 μm, 1.6 μm, and 6.7 μm.
The absorptivity of the first two peaks at 1.3 μm and 1.6 μm reached 98% and 96%, respectively.
The third absorption peak at 6.7 μm also reached an absorptivity of 96%.
The broadband absorption in the 1-2 μm range exceeded 80% due to multiple excitations of surface plasmon.
The simultaneous excitation of electric and magnetic fields at the silver-dielectric interface led to the high absorption at the 6.7 μm wavelength.
The surface current distribution inside the MIM structure exhibits an inductor-capacitor (LC) like behavior, contributing to the enhanced absorption.
The far-field directivity analysis shows 0% backward scattering at the resonant wavelengths, indicating forward scattering of electromagnetic radiation.
The use of GaAs as the dielectric material instead of MgF2 improves the optical transparency and reduces the possibility of deterioration due to moisture exposure.
The designed MIM structure can effectively suppress the scattering of IR laser beams and reduce heat waves from the surface, fulfilling the requirements of IR stealth technology.
The numerical simulations were performed using the Finite-Difference-Time-Domain (FDTD) method in the CST microwave studio.
The plasmonic-based metamaterial with the MIM structure was designed for applications in the field of IR stealth technology.
